Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the parking lot collision
you reported in Baytown. Can you start by telling me where you were when it happened?
A: Sure. I was pulling out of a parking space near the grocery store entrance, moving slowly, maybe five miles an
hour.
Q: Had you come to a complete stop before you started backing out?
A: Yes, I checked my mirrors, looked over my shoulder, and waited for a car to pass before I moved.
Q: What happened next?
A: A pickup truck came down the lane behind the row of cars. It didn't seem to slow down much, and it clipped the
rear corner of my car as I was backing out.
Q: Did you see the truck before the impact?
A: I saw headlights for a second, but I didn't realize how fast it was coming until it hit me.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, I got out and spoke with the other driver. He said he didn't see me. We exchanged insurance information.
Q: Did you feel any injuries right away?
A: Not really at first. I felt a little stiff, but by that evening my neck was sore and I had headaches. The next morning I
could barely turn my head to the left.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since the collision?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the following day, and they diagnosed whiplash. I've been doing physical
therapy twice a week since then.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about how the accident happened?
A: Only that I was being careful. I wasn't in a hurry, and I did everything I could to avoid it.
Q: Thank you. That concludes our statement for now.
</page>
